hints.title: Find the central angle from the area
hints.body: Triangle POQ has two sides of length 6. Use 12absinC for its area, then apply the given restriction on the central angle.
hints.recap: A sine value alone can correspond to two angles inside a triangle.
hints.pitfall: Do not choose the acute angle automatically.
hints.pause: Determine the central angle consistent with every condition.

recall.reminder: The sine-area formula uses two sides and their included angle.

hints.title: Split the chord into two right triangles
hints.body: Draw the perpendicular from the centre to chord PQ. It bisects both the chord and the isosceles triangle formed by the two radii.
hints.recap: The half-chord and the centre-to-chord distance can be calculated in a right triangle.
hints.pitfall: Use half of the central angle in that right triangle.
hints.pause: Find the chord length and its perpendicular distance from the centre.

recall.reminder: A perpendicular from the centre of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

hints.title: Keep the base fixed and move the third vertex
hints.body: With PQ fixed, the area depends only on the perpendicular distance of R from the chord. Consider the two ends of the diameter perpendicular to the chord.
hints.recap: Maximum area over a fixed base means maximum altitude.
hints.pitfall: The centre-to-chord distance must be combined with the radius on the correct side of the chord.
hints.pause: Choose the farthest permitted vertex, calculate its altitude, and then calculate the triangle area.

recall.reminder: For a fixed base, triangle area is proportional to its perpendicular height.

solution:
Put θ=∠POQ. From the given area, 12·6·6sinθ=93, so sinθ=3/2. The stated obtuse-or-right restriction selects θ=2π/3.

Let S be the midpoint of chord PQ. Then OS⟂PQ and bisects the central angle. Therefore OS=6cos(π/3)=3 and PQ=12sin(π/3)=63.

The base PQ is fixed. The greatest perpendicular distance of a point of the circle from this chord is OS+6=9, attained on the line through O perpendicular to the chord, on the side away from it. Hence the greatest area is 12·63·9=273. Answer D.
knowledgePattern: Recover an obtuse central angle, then maximise altitude above a fixed chord
